Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

surge complexconstraints · evaluates: The ComplexConstraints README evaluates each prompt in a single completion without tools and grades criteria independently using an LLM judge; it reports strict all-criteria task pass rate separately from the average fraction of criteria satisfied.

Permanent record ID: candidate.add17.complexconstraints.evaluation.v2

  • Its model-family override warning says proxy-served model names can silently lose reasoning controls; the declared configuration is part of the evaluation scope.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

surge complexconstraints · human annotation: ComplexConstraints’ v3 construction uses expert prompt/reference authoring, rubric authoring, second-expert review and senior adjudication, with iterative judge calibration checking both a hand-graded reference and an edited response whose correct verdict flips.

Permanent record ID: candidate.add17.complexconstraints.expert-pipeline.v2

  • This is a creator-reported benchmark construction procedure, not an independent review receipt for these research assertions.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

surge complexconstraints · trained on: The ComplexConstraints v3 paper describes Qwen 3-4B instruction-following RL training on a90:10 split of the companion set, about nine hundred training tasks, using GPT-5-mini criterion judgments and fraction-of-required-criteria reward.

Permanent record ID: candidate.add17.complexconstraints.training-scope.v2

  • This is the paper’s training recipe, not a new rerun or performance claim; external benchmarks were excluded from its stated training, tuning and selection procedure.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

surge complexconstraints · dataset size: The ComplexConstraints v3 paper defines a seventy-five-prompt benchmark with 1,559 criteria and a disjoint one-thousand-prompt companion training set; both contain single-turn tasks with ten to forty criteria per prompt.

Permanent record ID: candidate.add17.complexconstraints.units.v2

  • The creator blog describes fifteen to forty rubric items, whereas the paper and README say ten to forty; these descriptions remain version-specific. Training and evaluation sets are manifestations of one family.
